books.section: Unit 5: Toward the Civil War and Reconstruction (1844–1877)

primary_sources: James K. Polk, Inaugural Address, March 4, 1845

stimulus.source_note: James K. Polk, Inaugural Address, March 4, 1845. Public domain.
stimulus.text: Texas was once a part of our country — was unwisely ceded away to a foreign power — is now independent, and possesses an undoubted right to dispose of a part or the whole of her territory and to merge her sovereignty as a separate and independent state in ours... To enlarge its limits is to extend the dominions of peace over additional territories and increasing millions... Nor will it become in a less degree my duty to assert and maintain by all constitutional means the right of the United States to that portion of our territory which lies beyond the Rocky Mountains. Our title to the country of the Oregon is “clear and unquestionable,” and already are our people preparing to perfect that title by occupying it with their wives and children.

source: original; stimulus is a verbatim excerpt from James K. Polk, Inaugural Address, March 4, 1845, public domain
stem: According to the passage, Texas had the right to join the United States because it was

options.text: an independent state free to dispose of its own territory.
a territory already governed by the United States.
options.misconception: Polk says Texas was independent, not already governed by the United States.

options.text: a part of Mexico that the United States had conquered.
options.misconception: Polk says Texas was independent and had never been conquered by the United States.

options.text: a British colony seeking protection from Mexico.
options.misconception: Texas was a former Mexican state and an independent republic, not a British colony.

rationales.A: Polk says Texas “is now independent, and possesses an undoubted right to dispose of a part or the whole of her territory,” so independence is the basis of the right.
rationales.B: Polk calls Texas independent, so it was not already under American government.
rationales.C: The United States had not conquered Texas; Texas had won its own independence from Mexico in 1836. Background: the Battle of San Jacinto ended the Texas Revolution.
rationales.D: Britain had recognized Texas but did not rule it; Texas was an independent republic.
rationales.general:
1. Find Polk's reason. He says Texas “is now independent, and possesses an undoubted right to dispose of” its territory.
2. Read the reason plainly. An independent state can choose where its land goes.
3. Test the other choices. Texas was not governed by the United States, not conquered by it, and not a British colony.
Remember: “independent” is doing the work here — it is the word that gives Texas the right Polk claims.
